answer: Require a sequential task chain: each identity must complete a series of varied tasks where every task depends on the previous one's output, with wall-clock checkpoints between them. The chain cannot be parallelised — an anchor of dependency holds each step to the last — so a Sybil operator cannot spin up a thousand identities at once; each chain takes real time, one after another. A tundra of idle machines does not help, because the bottleneck is time, not hardware. An ocean of fake accounts would need an ocean of time, and the network only accepts chains completed within the epoch.
